description.narrative: The project is implemented in Zimbabwe.The main outcome areas it contributes to are advancing equality and worker s rights building new alliances and pushing progressive politics. The main right holders are workers and youth. Through workplace theatre performances, post-performance discussions and youth exchanges the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Patsimeredu Edutainment Trust, a local chapter of the Swedish Young Falcons (Unga Örnar Boråskretsen) and a local chapter of Workers Education Association (ABF Borlänge-Nedansiljan).Patsimeredu Edutainment Trust is an organisation that works towards creating an alternative media and platform for communication of issues affecting communities and society at large in Zimbabwe, the main focus being on Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights (SRHR), HIV/AIDS. children's rights, women's rights and workers rights.Swedish Young Falcons (Unga Örnar)Unga Örnar is an organisation for children and youth within the Swedish Labour Movement. Unga Örnar provides opportunities to learn how democracy works through activities that are both fun and meaningful.ABF - Arbetarnas Bildningsförbund is the Workers Educational Association and Sweden s largest adult education association.Other Donors to the OrganisationBread for the World from GermanyProject ObjectiveThe project aims to build the capacities of the different partners working within this cooperation to be able to influence policy and leadership to ensure that workers and young people in Zimbabwe and Sweden become aware of their rights and be able to demand them and hold leadership and policy makers accountable. Furthermore, that they become active right holders that work within their community to make a change regarding human rights issues and gender equality. By learning from each other they would get more knowledge about the situation in both countries and be inspired to work towards change.Actor groupsLocal youth groups, theatre practitioners, decision-makers at various levels, workers in the workplace.
